answer: A gas compressor station vibrates at frequencies tied to its running pumps, so a claimant nearby records the vibration spectrum and its dominant peak must match the station's operating log for that hour. The peak shifts when pumps start and stop, and those changes are logged publicly, so copied spectra fail the shift check; a river of identical claims dries up, a relic of one old spectrum cannot pass, and a sable dark control room sees the same peak only within a short radius, so a farm claiming many districts would need a sensor beside every station.
